arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case's counsel argued Arizona requires ineffective assistance claims in postconviction proceedings.
the opposing side's counsel argued the state rule is a valid procedural default.
Justice Ginsburg questioned the rationale for the state rule.
Justice Alito asked about the right to counsel for late-arising claims.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a state procedural rule bars federal courts from reviewing ineffective assistance claims. the side that brought the case seeks federal review. the opposing side seeks to uphold the state rule.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants federal courts to review the ineffective assistance claim despite the state procedural default.
the opposing side wants the state procedural rule to bar federal review of the claim.

paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the state rule creates an independent barrier to federal review of constitutional claims.
the opposing side argues the state rule is a valid procedural default that bars federal review.
